c. 1944
The following is a faithful transcription of a printed description and recipe for Baked Beans written by the Servant of God, Father Solanus Casey O. F.M. Cap.
(Father Solanus supplied not only the recipe for Baked Beans printed in the Eucharistic Mission Band Cook Book, but he also wrote a introduction and described his own experience, found on page 60 - EMB Cook Book, pub- lished in 1945.).
BAKED BEANS
Like potatoes, beans may be served in almost innumerable ways with good advantage at once to the cook and the guest. From the following actual experience of the writer may be culled a practical recipe for preparing and serving -- Real Boston Baked Beans.
A certain monastery in charge of a struggling parish, wishing in a way to forestall the financial drain often consequent on Thanksgiving Dinners, proclaimed to friends near and far the staging of a real Boston Baked Beans Dinner. This was to be just a week ahead of the great tur- key Thursday.
The Inspector himself was given the privilege of superintending the beans, supposed to be at once the staple feature of the repast and the highlight of the meal.
Priding himself more or less on the distinction, his first step was to get in touch with and have an understanding with the amiable Brother Cook (Wendlin) at the Monastery. They decided to put the beans to soak the Sunday night instead of Tuesday before the dinner. In that way they figured on about a good half-hour in a hot oven for the dinner Thursday evening.
They boiled them according to the recipe below and had them in the best condition Monday evening. When others sampled them the next morning they seemed even further improved. "Unsurpassable," was the word. Three days to wait for their grand display seemed long, but we were con- tent - confident that the delay would not lessen their value and appre- ciation.
But our pride, however legitimate it may have been, was to get a really practical jolt. Thursday morning finally came and was ideal - could hardly be more promising for a successful affair that night. So wishing to further cooperate with Brother Cook, the inspector made his way to the monastery kitchen. Brother, too was in best of smiles as they met at the kitchen door. But :
